text.de: Adolf Anderssen spielte diese freie Partie 1851 in London, am Rande des ersten internationalen Schachturniers. Er gab beide Türme, einen Läufer und zuletzt die Dame und setzte mit seinen verbliebenen Leichtfiguren matt. Wenige Jahre später erhielt sie den Namen „die Unsterbliche Partie“.
text.en: Adolf Anderssen played this casual game in London in 1851, alongside the first international chess tournament. He gave up both rooks, a bishop and finally his queen, then mated with his remaining minor pieces. A few years later it was given the name “the Immortal Game”.

text.de: Im Finalwettkampf des ersten Amerikanischen Schachkongresses 1857 traf Paul Morphy auf Louis Paulsen. Mit dem Damenopfer 17…Dxf3 riss er die Stellung des weißen Königs auf und gewann den folgenden Angriff. Morphy gewann das Turnier und galt danach als stärkster Spieler Amerikas.
text.en: In the final match of the 1st American Chess Congress in 1857, Paul Morphy faced Louis Paulsen. With the queen sacrifice 17…Qxf3 he tore open the white king’s position and won the ensuing attack. Morphy won the event and was then regarded as the strongest player in America.

text.en: Henry Bird and Paul Morphy played this game in London in 1858, during Morphy’s European tour. After White castled queenside, Morphy gave up a rook with 17…Rxf2 and later the second one to hunt the white king. The game shows how Morphy used open lines against the king.

text.en: Johannes Zukertort won the strong London tournament of 1883, and this game against Joseph Henry Blackburne is his best known. His queen move 28.Qb4 started a combination after which Blackburne’s position collapsed.

text.de: Der junge Emanuel Lasker spielte diese Partie 1889 in Amsterdam gegen Johann Hermann Bauer. Mit 15.Lxh7+ und 17.Lxg7 opferte er beide Läufer, um den schwarzen König freizulegen, und gewann danach Material. Das doppelte Läuferopfer wurde zum Vorbild für viele spätere Kombinationen dieser Art.
text.en: The young Emanuel Lasker played this game in Amsterdam in 1889 against Johann Hermann Bauer. With 15.Bxh7+ and 17.Bxg7 he sacrificed both bishops to strip the black king, then won material. The double bishop sacrifice became the model for many later combinations of this kind.

text.de: Diese Italienische Partie spielte der frühere Weltmeister Wilhelm Steinitz 1895 in Hastings. Nach 22.Txe7+ bot sein Turm sich immer wieder zum Schlagen an, ohne dass Schwarz ihn nehmen konnte. Curt von Bardeleben verließ nach dem 25. Zug den Saal, ohne aufzugeben, und Steinitz zeigte den Zuschauern das Matt.
text.en: Former world champion Wilhelm Steinitz played this Italian Game at Hastings in 1895. After 22.Rxe7+ his rook kept offering itself without Black being able to take it. Curt von Bardeleben left the hall after move 25 without resigning, and Steinitz showed the spectators the mate.

text.en: Akiba Rubinstein played this game against Georg Rotlewi in Lodz in 1907. His bishops aimed at the white king, and with 22…Rxc3 and 23…Rd2 he offered rook and queen until mate could not be stopped. It is often called “Rubinstein’s Immortal”.

text.en: Frank Marshall played this French Defence against Stepan Levitsky in Breslau in 1912. His final move 23…Qg3 puts the queen where it can be taken three ways, yet every capture loses for White. Legend has it that spectators showered the board with gold coins.

text.de: In der Endrunde von St. Petersburg 1914 musste Weltmeister Emanuel Lasker gegen José Raúl Capablanca gewinnen. Er wählte die als remislich geltende Abtauschvariante der Spanischen Partie und gewann mit einem Springer auf e6 und einem Angriff am Königsflügel. Lasker gewann das Turnier knapp vor Capablanca.
text.en: In the final stage of St. Petersburg 1914, world champion Emanuel Lasker needed a win against José Raúl Capablanca. He chose the Exchange Variation of the Ruy Lopez, considered drawish, and won with a knight on e6 and a kingside attack. Lasker won the tournament just ahead of Capablanca.

text.en: In this 1918 Ruy Lopez Frank Marshall first played the pawn sacrifice 8…d5 against José Raúl Capablanca, which is now called the Marshall Attack. Capablanca accepted the sacrifice, beat off the attack and won with the extra material.

text.en: Aaron Nimzowitsch played this Queen’s Indian against Friedrich Sämisch in Copenhagen in 1923. At the end White still has all his pieces, but every move worsens his position, and Sämisch resigned after 25…h6. It is known as the “Immortal Zugzwang Game”.

Im späten Mittelspiel setzte Aljechin eine lange Kombination mit Springer- und Turmzügen um, die mit Materialgewinn endete. Aljechin gewann das Turnier.
text.en: Richard Réti opened this game at Baden-Baden in 1925 with 1.g3, and Alexander Alekhine answered with an early central pawn advance. In the late middlegame Alekhine carried out a long combination with knight and rook moves that ended in a material gain. Alekhine won the tournament.

text.en: Max Euwe and Alexander Alekhine played this 26th game of the 1935 world championship match in Zandvoort, hence the name “Pearl of Zandvoort”. Euwe won it against the Dutch Defence with a middlegame combination. At the end of the match he became world champion.

text.en: Thirteen-year-old Robert James Fischer played this Grünfeld against Donald Byrne in New York in 1956. With 17…Be6 he gave up his queen and got so much material and attack in return that he delivered mate in the end. Chess journalist Hans Kmoch called it “the Game of the Century”.

text.en: Rashid Nezhmetdinov played this game against Lev Polugaevsky in Sochi in 1958. With 24…Rxf4 he left his queen to be taken and then drove the white king to the edge of the board with rook, knights and pawns. It is one of Nezhmetdinov’s best known attacking games.

text.en: Mikhail Tal played this Caro-Kann against former world champion Vasily Smyslov in the 1959 Candidates Tournament. He gave up a bishop for the attack, and with 16.Nh6+ and 17.Qxh5 forced a winning endgame. Tal won the tournament and played for the title in 1960.

text.en: In the sixth game of the 1960 title match Mikhail Tal played the King’s Indian against world champion Mikhail Botvinnik. His knight sacrifice 21…Nf4 opened lines against the white king, and Tal went on to win the endgame. Tal won the match and became world champion.

Byrne gab in einer Stellung auf, die mehrere Großmeister im Kommentarraum noch für Weiß günstig hielten. Fischer gewann das Turnier mit 11 aus 11.
text.en: Robert James Fischer played this game against Robert Byrne in the 1963/64 US Championship. A knight sacrifice on f2 opened the white king’s position. Byrne resigned in a position that several grandmasters in the commentary room still judged favourable for White. Fischer won the event with 11 out of 11.

text.en: In the 1965 Candidates semifinal the score was level before the tenth game. Against Bent Larsen’s Sicilian Mikhail Tal sacrificed a knight with 16.Nd5, whose soundness was debated for a long time. Tal won the game and the match.

text.en: In the tenth game of the 1966 title match Boris Spassky played the King’s Indian against world champion Tigran Petrosian. Petrosian gave up the exchange twice and finished the game with the queen sacrifice 30.Qh8+. He defended his title in this match.

text.en: In game 19 of the 1969 title match world champion Tigran Petrosian played the Sicilian against Boris Spassky. Spassky attacked on the kingside, and after 24 moves the game was decided. Spassky won the match and became world champion.

text.en: In the sixth game of 1972 Robert James Fischer opened with 1.c4, which he had hardly ever played before. He won a Queen’s Gambit with clear play against Boris Spassky’s hanging pawns. After the game Spassky joined in the applause.

text.en: The third game of the 1972 title match was played, at Fischer’s request, in a back room without spectators. With the unusual 11…Nh5 Fischer accepted weaknesses in his pawn structure and won. It was his first win ever against Boris Spassky.

text.en: In the 16th game of the 1985 title match Garry Kasparov sacrificed a pawn early against world champion Anatoly Karpov. His knight on d3 then paralysed White’s pieces, and Kasparov won. At the end of the match he became world champion.

text.en: In the 20th game of the 1990 title match Garry Kasparov attacked on the kingside in a Ruy Lopez. With knights and queen he broke through against the black king and finally won material. Kasparov defended his title against Anatoly Karpov in this match.
